reachable: Yes, on both additions, and both get gradient. (A) The retracted group resolves on the real genome to exactly the six (64,176) tensors the hypothesis names — file_read, file_write, path_read, path_write, tr_path, sys_val (enumerated by instantiating the r22 arch + r20 head and applying the impl's own selection rule). Five of those are the delta-rule addressing maps that produce q/k for _chunked_delta_reads and the tr_path key for _transition_reads (r18 arch lines 250, 324-330), i.e. exactly the machinery that decides what a read at a location returns at the scored position; they are trained by Muon on real gradients, unchanged from the parent. The retraction is a post-step projection, so it does not remove gradient, it constrains where the weight lands. Measured effect is large and matches the hypothesis: after 300 synthetic steps sigma_max/sigma_min is 1.002 for all six under this optim vs 3.62-11.74 under the parent optim (author claimed 3.44-4.12 vs 1.00); on real data (data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd, 40 steps, full genome through evolve.harness._train) 1.013-1.020, all params finite, ok=True. (B) Write-back reaches the returned net: the harness calls opt.step() exactly `steps` times (harness.py:79-112) and steps=4000 (eval/adapter.py:111), so the plateau index is 3000, the averager accumulates exactly 1001 iterates all at lr = 0.15*peak = 7.5e-5, and writes them into the live parameters on the final step, followed by retract(rate=1.0) and the cap. Ablating write_back to a no-op at 120 steps changes the returned weights by 0.5% global relative L2 (up to 4.7% on comp_out / film_out), so the averaged weights, not the last iterate, are what gets scored.
solves_outside_model: No — this is as clean as the axis gets. The whole 287-line impl imports only math and torch; it never receives, opens or parses a trajectory, a command string, a path, an mv edge or a batch. I read every line and checked for any data access: the only inputs are the parameter list and `steps`, and the only decisions taken are on p.ndim / p.shape / p.data values. Nothing in it can compute or inject the routing answer; it cannot even see a sample. Contrast with the retracted stream from last round: there is no path here from move-chain resolution to a model input, because there is no model input here at all. Selection of the six retracted tensors is by shape and sibling-count, not by name and not by any property of the data.
summary: The invented mechanism is implemented as described and I confirmed nearly every checkable claim by execution rather than reading. The tensor group is exactly the six (64,176) matrices the author names (including sys_val, which they disclose as an acknowledged over-inclusion). The retraction W <- (1-eta)W + eta*Q*||W||_F/||Q||_F with eta=0.2 and 6 Newton-Schulz iterations is coded verbatim and empirically drives sigma_max/sigma_min from 3.6-11.7 (parent optim) to ~1.00 within tens of steps, reproduced both on synthetic batches through the real arch and on the real data root through the real harness. The schedule is warmup / hold / cosine-to-floor-by-step-3000 / constant-0.15 thereafter; the averaging window coincides exactly with the constant-LR set (1001 iterates at 7.5e-5 at the 4000-step budget), write-back fires on the final step, is followed by retract(rate=1.0) and the spectral cap as claimed, and materially changes the returned weights. Degenerate budgets (1, 2, 5, 12, 30, 100, 400, 1000) all run without error and the write-back path executes. The diff against the parent optim is exactly the two additions plus floor_ratio 0.05 -> 0.15, with no touch to Muon, the spectral cap, or the group-selection rule; the parent's no-surface fallbacks were removed but the degrade path still holds (empty key list -> muon None and all params to AdamW; empty dd list -> cap is a no-op loop). Speed: +1.6 ms/step optimizer-only on CPU here vs the author's claimed +2.4 ms/step in-jail — same order, and they correctly label the GPU fraction unmeasured. Section-1 provenance is accurate for arch (r22 literally subclasses r18) and head (r20 imports the r18 head as CH, calls CH.wrap/_mine_triples/_smoothstep/_interleave_layout_ok and reproduces the r18 arm's math verbatim before adding the mem-pre arm), and slightly overstated for the batcher. Only two minor divergences, both narrative rather than mechanical. Section 3's safety argument also checks out: Q in _quotient is the verb basis, independent of the retracted weights, so _quotient and _unit make the addressing path exactly scale-invariant and the Frobenius rescale is indeed inert there. WHAT I COULD NOT CHECK: (1) whether any of this moves comp_ca — I did not run the real eval (4000 steps, and the eval is noisy at the 0.0227 floor anyway); (2) whether the addressing maps genuinely rank-collapse on the real training distribution under the parent, which is the hypothesis's core premise — my runs show parent condition numbers of 3.6-11.7, elevated and growing on tr_path but not catastrophic, and the author explicitly flags this as unmeasured; (3) the real-data effect of orthogonalizing sys_val's tanh path over a full 4000-step run; (4) GPU wall-clock overhead. Cleanup: I modified nothing in the repo (git status clean); all scripts live in /tmp/r3s4/ (mech.py, sched.py, wb.py, real.py) and nothing was installed.

divergences.claim: Section 2(A): "the fixed point of this map is the set of row-orthonormal 64x176 matrices: the Stiefel manifold St(176,64)".
divergences.what_the_code_does: Because the polar factor is rescaled to ||W||_F, the fixed points are scalar multiples of row-orthonormal matrices (all 64 singular values equal ||W||_F/8), i.e. the cone over St(176,64), not St(176,64) itself. In a real 40-step run the converged singular value is ~4.45/8 = 0.56, not 1. The condition-number claim (kappa -> 1) is exactly right; only the manifold label is loose. The hypothesis writes the rescale explicitly into its own update equation and argues the scale is cosmetic because every consumer of these maps is _unit-normalized, so this is imprecise naming rather than a mechanism mismatch.
divergences.evidence: optim__r3_stiefel_addressing_plateau_tailavg.py:88-100 (fro = ||W||; o = o * fro/||o||). Measured: after 100 retractions of an ill-conditioned 64x176, cond 316 -> 1.0000 with ||W||_F stable at 1.963 and sigma_max 0.245 (scaled orthonormal). Real-data 40-step run: cond 1.013-1.020, fro 4.44-4.48 (sigma ~ 0.56).

divergences.claim: Section 1: the batcher axis is a superset — "r2 ... builds the same image pools (img_pools, sampled by size, ramped hard_frac_max)" so "with coll_share=0.5 the parent's batcher already emits the partner's image-block behaviour half the time".
divergences.what_the_code_does: r2's image block is a tilted variant of r6's, not the same behaviour. r6 (evolve/chunks/batcher/r6_sysblock_hardneg_curriculum.py:11-30) picks k images and draws members uniformly; r2 (evolve/chunks/batcher/r2_routedepth_tilt_readcollision_blocks.py:116-162) samples the image group proportional to pool size and then draws members with a Boltzmann tilt on hop-count depth (tilted_pick). Same family, different sampling law. This is a provenance claim about two archived impls the candidate merely selects, not about the invented mechanism.
divergences.evidence: r2 line 162: parts.append(tilted_pick(img_pools[gi], m, alpha)) vs r6's uniform draw from pools; r2 lines 119-126 size-weighted group choice.
